LESSON: RHYTHM

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS
Strand: Creating and Executing
Topic 1.3: Rhythm

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Rhythm. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can rhythmic patterns be created?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. create rhythms using music note symbols and their rests
2. write in calligraphy French rhythm names of a rhythmic pattern
3. compose simple rhythms in two-beat patterns

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: RHYTHM
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Rhythm helps you succeed in CREATIVE ARTS. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: RHYTHM
Study Rhythm like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Create rhythms using music note symbols and their rests

What this means
In this part you learn to create rhythms using music note symbols and their rests. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: create rhythms using music note symbols and their rests.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Rhythm” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can create rhythms using music note symbols and their rests. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Write in calligraphy French rhythm names of a rhythmic pattern

What this means
In this part you learn to write in calligraphy French rhythm names of a rhythmic pattern. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: write in calligraphy French rhythm names of a rhythmic pattern.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Rhythm in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can write in calligraphy French rhythm names of a rhythmic pattern. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Compose simple rhythms in two-beat patterns

What this means
In this part you learn to compose simple rhythms in two-beat patterns. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: compose simple rhythms in two-beat patterns.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can compose simple rhythms in two-beat patterns. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Rhythm is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Rhythm” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: create rhythms using music note symbols and their rests)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Rhythm in your own words. (skill: write in calligraphy French rhythm names of a rhythmic pattern)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: compose simple rhythms in two-beat patterns)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Rhythm to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: create rhythms using music note symbols and their rests.
3. Practise this skill: write in calligraphy French rhythm names of a rhythmic pattern.
4. Practise this skill: compose simple rhythms in two-beat patterns.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Rhythm from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Rhythm: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study Rhythm?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can rhythmic patterns be created?
2. Why is calligraphy lettering used in writing?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Rhythm means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: create rhythms using music note symbols and their rests.
5. Be able to: write in calligraphy French rhythm names of a rhythmic pattern.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
